title: Carve include-conformance vector
description: One golden vector for the cross-engine file-inclusion conformance suite (PART 9 §19). Input fields describe the in-memory or on-disk fixture and the resolver/runtime options; `expected` holds the four golden outputs produced by the reference engine.

name.description: Unique vector id; also the file basename.

description.description: One-line human summary of what the vector pins.

rules.description: The §19 rule ids this vector exercises (I1..I14, plus I9a and the pseudo-rules 'multi-directive' and 'quoted-path').

mode.description: 'virtual' serves an in-memory files map; 'filesystem' materializes a real tree under a tmp dir and uses the fileSystemResolver.

resolver.description: 'none' configures no resolver (I3 literal case); 'virtual' serves the files map; 'filesystem' uses the fileSystemResolver over the materialized tree.

entry.description: virtual mode: the top-level document source.

files.description: virtual mode: the in-memory filesystem, mapping a path (as written in a directive) to its Carve/text source.

tree.description: filesystem mode: files and symlinks to materialize under a fresh tmp base. A string value is file content; a {symlink} object is a symbolic link whose target is resolved relative to the tree base.

entryPath.description: filesystem mode: which tree file is the top-level document.

root.description: filesystem mode: the containment root, relative to the tree base ('.' means the base itself).

sourcePath.description: Identity of the top-level document for warning attribution (I4). In filesystem mode, defaults to the real entry path; '<ENTRY>' requests that explicit default.

allowAbsolute.description: filesystem mode: allow absolute include paths after containment checks.

resolverIds.description: virtual mode: the resolver strips a leading './' and returns a canonical id, so two spellings of one file collapse (I6/I11 identity).

resolverThrows.description: virtual mode: the resolver throws this message, exercising the I7 path where the raw error must stay out of the normalized warning.

forbiddenSubstrings.description: Substrings that MUST NOT appear in any warning message (I7 no-leak). Checked against raw messages by the runner.

checkFmtExpandEquivalence.description: When true, the runner also asserts that expanding the FORMATTED entry yields the same html + dependency set as expanding the original (I12 stronger invariant).

expected.description: The four golden outputs, produced by the reference engine and regenerated by scripts/gen-include-conformance.mjs.

fmt.description: The Carve serializer output of the PRE-EXPANSION document (pins I12/I14 -- the directive survives formatting).

warnings.description: Normalized warnings in document order. Each is { rule, file? }; message/detail/positions are deliberately excluded (see README normalization).

dependencies.description: Normalized dependency set in first-encounter order (I11 contract). Each is { id, resolved }.
